reason: The image-only reading was already close; the reread on the image with the Vulgate at hand settled the oddly formed 'dominus' on canvas 1 line 4 and the trimmed last lines, and fixed the lesson divisions to verses.
sources: Biblia sacra iuxta Latinam Vulgatam versionem, vol. V, Samuhel (Rome, 1944), pp. 102-103 (1 Sam 7:7-17) and 105-106 (8:8-9:1), with apparatus; archive.org bibliasacraiuxta0005unse, page images n121, n122, n124, n125
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-5xnq (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 205), made by a research reader on the native images with the Rome Vulgate vol. V at hand. All 33 lines of both faces were reread on the image; line 33 of each face is trimmed and only letter tops survive. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels. Expansions in parentheses; [ ] lost or supplied; ? uncertain; [T] = red/black double-barred lesson-end sign.
